title: Lesson 3 — Print Awareness / Concepts About Print
source: User-supplied WGU D669 Lesson 3 Print Awareness section
definition: Print awareness (concepts about print) means understanding that print carries meaning, that written language represents spoken language, and that print is organized according to conventions such as directionality and spaces between words.

concepts_about_print.label: Text has meaning
concepts_about_print.example: Recognize that the words on a page, not just pictures, represent a story or information

concepts_about_print.label: Book orientation
concepts_about_print.example: Identify front and back cover, title, author, and illustrator

concepts_about_print.label: Book directionality and handling
concepts_about_print.example: Hold and turn pages of a conventional English-language book

concepts_about_print.label: Text directionality
concepts_about_print.example: Follow English print from left to right, top to bottom

concepts_about_print.label: Knowledge of letters, words, and sentences
concepts_about_print.example: Recognize letters, spaces between words, and sentence boundaries

notes: Print functions vary by context: books tell stories and menus list choices.
Some children enter school knowing print conventions; others benefit from explicit modeling and practice.
Print awareness and the alphabetic principle are related but distinct: alphabetic principle connects letters/graphemes with sounds/phonemes.
Ehri's phases of word-reading development are mentioned in the course video; video contents were not transcribed or independently verified.
Directionality and page-turning conventions described apply to English-language books and are not universal to all writing systems.

before: Select an appropriate illustrated book with visible print and book features
Introduce title, author, illustrator and roles
Model cover orientation and appropriate book handling
during: Track print with a finger or pointer
Highlight spaces, punctuation, capital letters and sentence boundaries
Discuss pictures and their connection to text
Ask students to predict what comes next
after: Match letters or identify words in text
Invite children to handle and explore books
Discuss, summarize and reflect on the story

resources.title: Print Awareness and the Alphabetic Principle
resources.focus: Print concepts, alphabetic principle, Ehri's phases; connection to decoding and spelling

reflection_questions: How do print awareness and the alphabetic principle support a child's movement toward accurate decoding?
How does recognizing print as spoken language affect children's literacy development?
How can teachers strengthen children's print awareness during read-alouds?

activity.prompt: Choose the correct stage of reading for each teaching move.

items.prompt: Introduce the story by stating the title, then the author's name and asking students, 'What does an author do?'
items.explanation: This establishes context and introduces the author before the text begins.

items.prompt: Select vocabulary words from the story you want to introduce.
items.explanation: Preteaching selected vocabulary helps students approach the story with relevant word meanings.

items.prompt: Briefly discuss the pictures on each page.
items.explanation: Discussing illustrations while reading supports engagement and comprehension.

items.prompt: Encourage students to guess or predict what will happen next.
items.explanation: Predicting during reading engages students in meaning-making.

items.prompt: Ask students to tell you if they liked the story and why.
items.explanation: Personal reflection after reading can encourage discussion and demonstrate engagement.

items.prompt: Summarize the story in a few brief points.
items.explanation: Summarizing after the story reinforces its important ideas.
